decisions.quote:
The present study, therefore, seeks to replicate the representative bureaucracy experi-

ment by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016), but using a different policy context:

emergency preparedness. Thus, the present study can be characterized as a concep-

tual replication or conceptual extension, rather than a direct or exact replication

(Makel, Plucker, and Hegarty 2012; Tsang and Kwan 1999).
decisions.reason: The study collects new experimental survey data from 604 US respondents in May 2015 to conceptually re-test the symbolic gender representation finding of Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016) in the domain of emergency preparedness, making it a replication.

decisions.quote:
Thus, whether combined or separately, male

and female participants were not influenced in any statistically significant way by the

variation in first names of Citizens Corps officials. Our experiment, in sum, produced

only null findings, in contrast to the original study by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li

(2016).
decisions.reason: With the tested original study resolved to Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016), the authors' explicit overall verdict is that their conceptual replication produced only null findings across all outcomes (willingness to donate time, money, and blood) and analytic models, in direct contrast to the positive symbolic representation effects reported in the original study. Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'failed'.
